scope: Persistent model residency and rolling camera-frame anchor smoke
summary: One Wan-Animate-2 process loaded the 14B model once and generated two overlapping 80-frame windows, using the previous result's local frame 64 as the second window's camera-frame identity anchor.
evidence: Physical A800 GPUs 1 and 4 completed both windows; model load was 115.9003 seconds, the cold compiled first window was 147.3037 seconds, and the resident second window was 68.5596 seconds.
Both results decode to 80 frames at 624x351 and 24 FPS.
Against the historical fixed-anchor pair, overlap same-time MAD decreased from 8.0367 to 6.0691 and best-seam MAD decreased from 7.5501 to 4.0747.
lessons: Keeping the model resident removes repeated 14B checkpoint loads, while an explicitly named source-camera continuation frame can reduce overlap disagreement without cross-dissolving identities.
limitations: This covers two windows rather than a complete 20-second-or-longer output.
The overlap comparison uses a historical fixed-anchor run from an earlier Python build and is not a perfectly isolated single-variable ablation.
Image-space continuity does not establish contact physics or real robot execution.
next_actions: Run all ten windows of the 27.5-second source on two independent GPU pairs and stitch/evaluate the complete output.
